en: One whose heart melts with compassion for all living beings has no need of knowledge, of freedom, of matted hair or of smearing ash on the body.
If a teacher teaches a pupil even one single letter, there is no wealth on earth that the pupil could give to repay that debt.
For wicked people and for thorns there are only two remedies: crush them with a shoe, or keep far away from them.
Good fortune leaves a person who wears dirty clothes, has unclean teeth, eats too much, speaks harshly, and sleeps at sunrise or sunset, even if he were Vishnu himself.
When a man loses his money, his friends, wife, servants and well-wishers leave him; when he is rich again, they come back. In this world, money is a man's true relative.
Wealth gained unjustly stays for ten years; when the eleventh year comes, it is lost along with its roots.

first: अयुक्तं स्वामिनो युक्तं युक्तं नीचस्य दूषणम् ।
en: What is wrong in a great person passes as right, and what is right in a low person is called a fault: nectar brought death to Rahu, while poison became an ornament for Shiva.
True food is what is left after the learned have eaten; true friendship is that shown to others; true wisdom is that which does no wrong; and true righteousness is that done without show.
A jewel may lie rolling at one's feet and glass may be worn on the head, but when it is time to buy and sell, glass is glass and a jewel is a jewel.
The scriptures are endless and there are many branches of learning, but time is short and obstacles are many; so take only the essence, as a swan takes the milk out of water.

first: दूरागतं पथि श्रान्तं वृथा च गृहमागतम् ।
en: One who eats without first honouring a guest who has come from far away, tired from the road, and arrived unexpectedly at his home is called an outcast.
Some read the four Vedas and many books of law, yet they do not know their own self, just as a ladle does not know the taste of the food it stirs.
Blessed is the boat of the twice-born, which works the other way round on the sea of worldly life: all who stay low cross over, and those who stay on top sink.

The moon is a store of nectar, lord of healing plants, with a body made of nectar and full of light; yet it loses its rays when it enters the sun's circle. Who does not become small when living in another's house?
This bee, which once lived among lotus petals, lazy and drunk on lotus nectar, now finds itself by fate in a strange land and thinks highly of the juice of the kutaja flower.

first: पीतः क्रुध्देन तातश्चरणतलहता वल्लभो येन रोषा-
en: (Lakshmi speaks:) One Brahmin in anger drank up my father, the ocean; another kicked my beloved in rage; from childhood the best Brahmins keep my rival, learning, in their mouths; and every day they cut my home, the lotus, to worship Shiva. So, my Lord, I am always unhappy and stay away from the homes of Brahmins.
There are many kinds of bonds, but the bond made by the rope of love is different: the bee, skilled at boring through wood, becomes helpless inside the closed lotus bud.

Even when cut, the sandalwood tree does not lose its scent; even when old, the king of elephants does not lose his playfulness; even when pressed in the mill, sugarcane does not lose its sweetness; and even when poor, a person of good family does not give up good character.

first: उर्व्यां कोऽपि महीधरो लघुतरो दोर्भ्यां धृतो लीलया
en: (Radha says to Krishna:) You playfully lifted some small mountain from the earth with your arms, and so in heaven and on earth you are always praised as the holder of Govardhana. I carry you, the holder of the three worlds, on my breast, yet no one counts that. Keshava, what is the use of more talk? Fame comes through good fortune.
